armSurfacesPrompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: original transparent game character arm-component atlas.
Input images: first image is front-view character/material reference; second is rear-view character/material reference. Preserve the cream rolled linen sleeves, fair adult female skin and dark leather bracer identity, but REBUILD the arm components with anatomically natural neutral wrist rotation for walking. Output a NEW isolated 4-column by 3-row grid of twelve parts, not complete people.

Columns: 1 anatomical LEFT arm seen from FRONT; 2 anatomical RIGHT arm seen from FRONT; 3 anatomical LEFT arm seen from BACK; 4 anatomical RIGHT arm seen from BACK. FRONT is a person walking directly toward camera; BACK walks directly away. Orthographic camera elevated 20 degrees. Same soft warm upper-left light and refined realistic game-render materials.

Row 1: four separate upper arms, cream linen rolled sleeves, shoulder at top, elbow at bottom. Straight relaxed upper arms with accurate shoulder caps and elbow ends aligned along a vertical centerline, no bent elbows baked into the cloth. The FRONT pair exposes the anterior sleeve/elbow crease, BACK pair posterior sleeve/elbow. No forearms or hands in this row.
Row 2: four separate neutral-rotation forearms, elbow top and wrist bottom, vertically aligned. Anatomical LEFT has the leather bracer, anatomical RIGHT is bare. Palms would face the THIGHS, not the camera or behind the body. Accurate inward-facing wrist edge, taper and soft anatomical volume. No hands in this row.
Row 3: four separate relaxed lightly curled hands with a short wrist at top, fingers downward, posed as though loosely encircling a slim vertical handle with the palm facing the thigh. Front view shows the thumb/radial edge, NOT a flat broad back of the hand. Rear view shows the outer/ulnar side and curled knuckles, thumb mostly hidden, clearly different from front. The FRONT left hand belongs on screen-right of the body, FRONT right on screen-left. BACK left is screen-left, BACK right screen-right. Hands must look correctly attached to relaxed hanging arms; no palm-forward anatomical display, no thumb pointing out away from body, no splayed fingers. No actual handle or weapon; leave an unobtrusive grip in the softly curled fingers.

All twelve components separately isolated with generous empty gutters. Anatomically accurate adult female hands, consistent proportions. Actual transparent alpha background everywhere between parts, no backdrop, no checkerboard, no glow, no floor, no labels, no lines, no numbers. Keep every component within its own cell.
neutralHandsPrompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: four isolated NEUTRAL GRIP HAND sprites for the Crownforge woman, actual transparent PNG.
Reference images provide skin/material style only. Do NOT copy their flat dorsal hand pose.
Primary request: render FOUR anatomically correct adult female hands, tightly framed but separate, in one horizontal row. Only hands and short wrists; NO arms, weapons, text or background.
All four wrists enter vertically from TOP, hand hangs DOWN, fingers softly CURLED into a relaxed C-shaped fist as if holding a narrow upright cylinder. Natural neutral forearm rotation: the PALM FACES THE THIGH/side of the torso. This is NOT a palm-forward or broad-back-of-hand view. This distinction is essential.

1: Anatomical LEFT hand seen by someone directly IN FRONT of a standing woman. It belongs on the RIGHT side of her front-view body. Palm faces inward toward screen-left. We see the THUMB EDGE toward camera: thumbnail and curled thumb dominate, knuckles recede behind. 
2: Anatomical RIGHT hand viewed from the FRONT. It belongs on the LEFT side of her front-view body. Palm faces inward toward screen-right. We see the THUMB EDGE toward camera: thumbnail and curled thumb dominate, knuckles recede behind.
3: Anatomical LEFT hand viewed from BEHIND. It belongs on the LEFT side of her back-view body. Palm faces inward toward screen-right. We see the LITTLE-FINGER EDGE toward camera, rounded curled finger stack, thumbnail concealed on opposite side.
4: Anatomical RIGHT hand viewed from BEHIND. It belongs on the RIGHT side of her back-view body. Palm faces inward toward screen-left. We see the LITTLE-FINGER EDGE toward camera, rounded curled finger stack, thumbnail concealed on opposite side.

Each hand slim and viewed nearly EDGE-ON (narrow silhouette), not a flat five-finger dorsal display. Closed curled fingers with natural knuckle folds, no long extended fingers pointing down. Keep empty handle space tiny and subtle; NO visible handle. Softly lit realistic fair-skinned adult female game anatomy, clean detailed edges, warm upper-left key light. Same character/style as references. Genuine transparent alpha background and wide empty separation; no ground, checkerboard, labels or detached fingers.
alphaExtractionPrompt:

Asset type: transparent PNG game sprite sheet
Primary request: Extract all separate character components from the supplied image onto a genuinely transparent background with an alpha channel.
Input image: edit target.
Constraints: keep every component and its placement, detail, color, facing direction and size unchanged. Remove only the painted checkerboard background. Preserve clean edges and all gaps. The output is a transparent cutout PNG, not an illustration of cutouts on paper.
notes: The arm atlas contributes only the first eight sleeve/forearm components. Its generated hand row is not used; neutral-hands.png supplies inspected curled hand surfaces. Original tool-produced PNGs are copied unchanged. No character view is mirrored.
